Trustworthy Evaluation of AI-Assisted Painting Restoration

Failure Taxonomy and Trustworthiness Flags

Transparent operational screening across validated reference, perceptual, feature, spatial, local, semantic, uncertainty, and statistical evidence.

Generated: 2026-09-01T21:50:44.028856Z

1. Executive summary

1,785 Union candidates
14 Transparent failure categories
11 Independent flags
165 Supported four-seed groups
2,266 Triggered category assignments
5,486 Triggered flag assignments

This report converts the validated metric evidence into explicit failure categories, independent trustworthiness flags, and candidate-level review recommendations. The rules expose why a candidate needs review instead of hiding evidence inside one aggregate value.

  • RQ1: model comparison is reported only for the matched primary comparison population.
  • RQ2: metric agreement and disagreement remain visible across evidence families and repair regions.
  • RQ3: repeated-seed uncertainty is reported only where four supported diffusion candidates exist.
Scope: The combined trust score is not used. Uncertainty is not calibrated confidence. These outputs provide decision support and do not constitute conservation approval.
Conclusion: The evidence supports candidate screening and targeted manual review. It does not support automatic acceptance, historical-authenticity claims, or a universal model ranking.

2. Evaluation population

The union contains 1,785 unique candidates. The matched primary comparison contains 1,230 candidates: 410 each for OpenCV Telea, LaMa, and Stable Diffusion. The repeated-seed population contains 660 Stable Diffusion candidates in 165 complete groups.

3. How to interpret the rules

Each candidate-category pair has one of four states: triggered, not triggered, insufficient evidence, or not applicable. Triggered means that the documented operational rule was met. It is not a human-labelled conservation diagnosis.

Assignment status Rows
not_triggered 17526
insufficient_evidence 4378
triggered 2266
not_applicable 820
  • A warning identifies adverse evidence under the documented rule.
  • A critical state increases review priority; it does not measure physical conservation severity.
  • Insufficient evidence never counts as a pass.
  • Not applicable is used when a concept does not apply, such as stochastic uncertainty for deterministic methods.
Conclusion: The rules are auditable screening decisions. They narrow the candidates requiring attention but cannot replace visual or specialist assessment.

5. Failure taxonomy overview

Fourteen categories cover reference error, semantic and structural inconsistency, texture and colour behaviour, seam evidence, outside-mask alteration, composition proxies, and repeated-seed instability.

Failure category Operational definition Proxy Trigger rule Required response
Residual masked-region error Reference error remains high inside the intended repair region. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect the repaired region against the clean reference and error map.
Excessive blur Local edges or surface variation are reduced beyond the operational screening threshold. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect edges and brushwork inside the repair crop.
Structural-collapse proxy Feature-affinity evidence indicates a possible loss or displacement of structural layout. True one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect major contours and spatial layout; seek specialist review when critical.
Semantic-inconsistency proxy Local feature evidence is less compatible with the clean reference inside the repair crop. True one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect whether repaired structures remain compatible with surrounding content.
Repeated-texture proxy Periodicity or generated-detail evidence indicates potentially artificial repeated texture. True one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect repeated motifs and generated-looking surface detail.
Texture smoothing Local texture variation appears flatter than the clean reference. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect whether original brushwork or surface variation was flattened.
Texture discontinuity Texture or gradient behaviour changes abruptly across the repaired area or boundary. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect texture continuity across the repair boundary.
Colour-bleeding proxy Colour discontinuity or spillover evidence indicates possible colour transfer across the boundary. True one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect colour transfer across the mask boundary.
Colour drift Colour difference evidence is adverse inside the repaired region. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect colour matching inside the restored region.
Boundary seam Gradient, orientation, or local-structure evidence indicates a visible repair transition. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect the boundary ring at full resolution.
Mask spillover The restoration changes pixels immediately outside the intended repair support. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect pixels immediately outside the intended repair.
Outside-mask alteration Pixels outside the intended mask change beyond the approved numerical tolerance. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Do not rely automatically; verify compositing and untouched content.
Composition-change proxy Global or outside-context feature evidence indicates possible broader layout change. True one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect global layout and unchanged context; seek specialist review when critical.
Unstable multi-seed completion Repeated stochastic candidates vary materially across independent evidence families. False one critical indicator or two distinct warning components Inspect all seeds together; do not select one attractive output without reporting variability.
Conclusion: Category-level reporting makes the reason for a failure decision visible. A candidate can perform well in one domain and still require review in another.

  • Low variability means the generated candidates are similar to one another, not necessarily correct.
  • High variability means that candidate selection is seed-sensitive and should not rely on one output.
  • Telea and LaMa are deterministic, so stochastic uncertainty is not applicable rather than zero.
  • SDXL has one seed per bounded case, so uncertainty evidence is insufficient.
Conclusion: Repeated-seed instability is a useful risk signal for diffusion restoration. It is not calibrated confidence and cannot determine whether a stable restoration is correct.

Every candidate receives exactly one recommendation: do not rely automatically, unstable candidate, specialist review required, or suitable for preliminary inspection.

Recommendation Candidates Population fraction

  • Do not rely automatically: critical blocker evidence is present.
  • Unstable candidate: supported repeated-seed evidence shows material instability.
  • Specialist review required: adverse, critical, or consequentially incomplete evidence needs expert inspection.
  • Suitable for preliminary inspection: no current rule requires a stronger restriction, but the result remains preliminary.
These recommendations are decision support only. Even the most favourable category is not conservation approval.
Conclusion: Recommendations define the next review action. They do not certify authenticity, historical plausibility, material safety, or museum readiness.

13. Internal consistency

The persisted ledgers contain one row for every candidate-category and candidate-flag pair: 24,990 failure assignments and 19,635 flag assignments.

  • Candidate, case, model, prompt, and population identities remain unchanged after CSV reload.
  • Flag definitions match the controlled configuration.
  • Supporting assignment and evidence identifiers resolve to known records.
  • Recommendation values remain identical across all eleven flag rows for each candidate.
  • Quantile ties and zero-threshold saturation were checked explicitly.
Conclusion: The taxonomy is reproducible from its persisted evidence and transparent rules. Internal consistency does not by itself validate the rules against human conservator judgement.

14. Thesis conclusions

RQ1 - How do restoration methods compare?

The matched 410-case-per-model population shows clear differences in triggered failure burden. The model with the lowest burden is better under these measured screening rules, while no result establishes universal superiority.

RQ2 - What do the evaluation metrics reveal?

Reference, perceptual, feature, spatial, texture, colour, seam, semantic, and statistical evidence expose different restoration weaknesses. Metric disagreement demonstrates that one strong score is not enough to accept a restoration.

RQ3 - What does generative uncertainty add?

Four-seed groups reveal when Stable Diffusion restoration is sensitive to random generation. This supports seed-aware review, but uncertainty is not calibrated confidence and stability is not correctness.

  • Transparent failure categories are more useful for review than one opaque score.
  • Visual repair-region inspection remains necessary.
  • Missing evidence must remain visible.
  • Bounded SDXL evidence should remain descriptive.
Overall conclusion: AI-assisted painting restoration can be evaluated more trustworthily when model comparisons, region-aware metrics, uncertainty, disagreement, missingness, and visual evidence remain separate and traceable.

15. Limitations and provenance

  • Failure assignments are transparent operational screening rules, not human-labelled or conservation-validated failures.
  • Warning and critical percentiles identify relative outliers and do not provide calibrated probabilities.
  • Semantic, structural, repeated-texture, colour-bleeding, composition-change, and visible-boundary categories remain computational proxies.
  • The 1,785-candidate union contains primary-comparison and uncertainty-only roles that must not be pooled for ordinary model comparison.
  • Prompt variants remain separate uncertainty populations and cannot be pooled as repeated seeds.
  • Telea and LaMa are deterministic, so stochastic uncertainty is not applicable rather than zero.
  • SDXL has one seed for ten selected cases, so stochastic uncertainty is insufficient rather than absent.
  • The bounded SDXL population is incomplete and cannot support a general model ranking.
  • Metric disagreement is informative evidence and must not be hidden by a combined score.
  • No flag or recommendation establishes historical authenticity, conservation suitability, or museum approval.

The categories named semantic inconsistency, structural collapse, composition change, repeated texture, colour bleeding, and visible boundary are computational proxy signals. They do not verify object identity, face anatomy, historical intent, material compatibility, or authenticity.
